newsitem.title: ITALY: Feline glamour stalks catwalks in Milan.
newsitem.headline: Feline glamour stalks catwalks in Milan.

text.p: Italian fashion designer Anna Molinari unveiled an autumn/winter womenswear collection of feminine flounces on Wednesday, while Chiara Boni invoked full-length feline glamour.

Boni's spectacle at the ready-to-wear shows for the 1997-98 season included a live radio broadcast by a male journalist sashaying down the catwalk in a black velvet suit as he spoke to local radio listeners.
Her collection exploited feather boas, tasselled elbow-length evening gloves, seamed stockings and leopardskin prints for an overall image of sensual glamour.
For daywear, traditional masculine pinstripes and flannels were used for ankle-length, column-like dresses cut close to move with the curves of the female form.

Boni also dressed men in rich velvet suits with vibrant monotone ties of warm red and gold to complement the women's garments, saying in a statement the idea was to let men "enjoy the caress of velvet, the delicate softness of silk."
"Let's make one thing quite clear -- a man is a man and a woman a woman. Yet their paths meet on my catwalk," Boni said.
Hemlines brushed the ankle, skirt splits rose provocatively high up the thigh and coats and jackets in shimmering tiger stripes and leopardskin honey-golden velvet topped outfits.

For evening, Boni displayed off-the-shoulder gowns in transparent but discreet burgundy or chocolate brown chiffon with flower patterns and ankle length monotone sheaths hemmed with filmstar-like feathers and ruffles.
She brought the show to a close with a glittering black transparent lacy mini-dress, set off by an extravagantly wide brimmed hat trimmed generously with layers of tulle.

Diminutive stylist Anna Molinari, showing her own-name designs on the fourth day of Milan fashion week, produced a characteristically feminine collection with short, bouncy evening gowns fluffed up with visible tulle petticoats.
Molinari cut skirt hems diagonally across the thigh and introduced a bustle-like tail by folding extra layers of silk or taffeta into the skirt at the back.
Colours were a mixture of pastel blues, aluminium greys, navy or cherry red for lacy evening gowns, as well as cocoa brown schoolgirlish frocks trimmed demurely in white at the collar and cuffs.
Knits came in chunky cocoa or sheer cream for wide-necked dresses and skirts which gently followed the body's contours.

Italian designer Krizia, whose real name is Mariuccia Mandelli, takes the wraps off her collection later on Wednesday while Giorgio Armani displays his second line Emporia Armani on Thursday. The shows close with Armani's top line on Sunday.

Celebrities so far have included U.S. jazz musician Ray Charles who performed during Salvatore Ferragamo's show on Tuesday, while Hollywood actress Greta Scacchi is due to appear at the Iceberg show later on Wednesday.
